preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 2 * 10**5 for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit()) and all(1 <= int(a) <= 10**12 for a in a_values) and all(1 <= int(w) <= 10**12 for w in offer_weights)
preconditions.description: Input consists of valid integers: n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2e5), m (0 ≤ m ≤ 2e5), a_i (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 1e12), and special offers (x, y, w) where 1 ≤ x, y ≤ n, x ≠ y, and 1 ≤ w ≤ 1e12. a_values and offer_weights are parsed from the input lines.
The input contains exactly n vertex values and m special offers, where n and m are the first two integers read.

preconditions.expression: all(x != y for x, y, w in offers)
preconditions.description: All special offers have distinct x and y (x ≠ y).

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer representing the minimum cost to connect the graph.

The output is the minimum total cost to connect all n vertices into a single connected component, where min_total_cost is computed by considering all possible edge additions (either via special offers or standard a_x + a_y costs) and selecting the minimum spanning tree (MST) cost.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= cost <= 10**12 for cost in edge_costs) and all(1 <= x <= n and 1 <= y <= n and x != y for x, y in edge_pairs)
postconditions.description: The edge costs and pairs used in the MST are valid: each edge cost is between 1 and 1e12, and each edge connects distinct vertices within the range 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: len(selected_edges) == n - 1 and all(connected(selected_edges) for selected_edges in possible_msts)
postconditions.description: The solution selects exactly n-1 edges (forming a spanning tree) that connect all n vertices, where connected(selected_edges) means the graph formed by selected_edges is connected.
